Keeping your mailing address current stays your own responsibility, so it is not something DMV does for you. If mail from DMV is going to an old address, that is on the driver to fix. So after any move, count ten days and make sure the change is in, either online or by mail, before that time runs out. Some drivers wait for a new card to show up in the mail after reporting a move, and it never comes, because none is sent automatically. Driving while your license is expired breaks the law, so knowing whether your card is valid matters every time you drive. We will look at how lost, stolen, or damaged licenses are renewed or replaced, the online path and the office fallback, the extra identity and signature rules DMV may apply when issuing a card, and what to do with an old card after the new one arrives. We will finish by sorting the three online routes so you always know where to start.","fact_ids":["sec04-F05","sec04-F06","sec04-F07","sec04-F09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Expired means do not drive","fact_ids":["sec04-F05","sec04-R05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Driving on an expired license breaks the law.","fact_ids":["sec04-F05","sec04-R05"]},{"text":"Expired cards forbid driving.","fact_ids":["sec04-F05","sec04-R05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Driving while your license is expired breaks the law. There is no grace period described in the handbook, so the moment your license expires, you should not drive on it. This is one half of a simple pair of rules about card validity. Expired cards forbid driving, and superseded cards, the old ones replaced by a new card, forbid keeping. We will meet the second half shortly. This fits the larger routing picture: license services for updates and reissues, the address change page for moves, and the field office as the fallback. Knowing the order saves time. Start online, and only head to an office when the online path is not open for your situation. Either way, the card you receive replaces the old one.","fact_ids":["sec04-F06","sec04-R03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u02-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Issuance rules","fact_ids":["sec04-F07","sec04-F08","sec04-R06"]},"lines":[{"text":"DMV may ask for extra identity proof.","fact_ids":["sec04-F07","sec04-F08","sec04-R06"]},{"text":"Matching expiry dates need a valid ID document.","fact_ids":["sec04-F07","sec04-F08","sec04-R06"]},{"text":"Minors need a parent signature.","fact_ids":["sec04-F07","sec04-F08","sec04-R06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Before issuing a license, DMV may demand extra identity proof. So issuance can bring two kinds of extra requirement: fresh identity proof when expiry dates collide, and a parent or guardian signature for minors. Check both before you apply. If you are a minor, bring the signature, and if your identity document is close to expiring, be ready to provide a valid one.","fact_ids":["sec04-F07","sec04-F08","sec04-R06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u02-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Three routes online","fact_ids":["sec04-R03","sec04-R01","sec04-F01","sec04-F03","sec04-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Updates and reissues: license services.","fact_ids":["sec04-R03","sec04-R01","sec04-F01","sec04-F03","sec04-F06"]},{"text":"Moves: address change page.","fact_ids":["sec04-R03","sec04-R01","sec04-F01","sec04-F03","sec04-F06"]},{"text":"Fallback: field office.","fact_ids":["sec04-R03","sec04-R01","sec04-F01","sec04-F03","sec04-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Let us put the routes together. The field office is the fallback when the online path is unavailable. It also helps to know what each action does. Use DMV license services for a legal name change or other license-detail update. Report a move within ten days so DMV can update the address on file; this does not automatically replace the license card, which you may request for a fee. So a move updates your address on file but does not reissue your card, while a replacement gives you a new card.","fact_ids":["sec04-R03","sec04-R01","sec04-F01","sec04-F03","sec04-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u02-s6","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"The spare card","fact_ids":["sec04-F09","sec04-F05","sec04-R05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Trap: keep the old card as a backup.","fact_ids":["sec04-F09","sec04-F05","sec04-R05"]},{"text":"Truth: it is void; destroy it.","fact_ids":["sec04-F09","sec04-F05","sec04-R05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a trap. When a lost card turns up after its replacement has arrived, it is tempting to keep it as a backup. But the old card stops being valid the moment the replacement arrives, so it should be destroyed. Remember the pair: expired cards forbid driving, and superseded cards forbid keeping. May they use the one-year extension?","fact_ids":["sec04-F11","sec04-R04"]},"answer":{"text":"No, limited-term licenses are barred from it.","fact_ids":["sec04-F11"]},"rationale":{"text":"The extension is for out-of-state drivers who cannot renew, but limited-term licenses are excluded.","fact_ids":["sec04-F11","sec04-R04"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec04-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Stuck out of state","fact_ids":["sec04-F10","sec04-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"A one-year extension may be possible.","fact_ids":["sec04-F10","sec04-R04"]},{"text":"Ask before the license expires.","fact_ids":["sec04-F10","sec04-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers a situation that catches some California drivers off guard: being out of state when the license is about to expire and being unable to renew in time. The handbook offers a one-year extension for these drivers, but there are conditions. The request has to be made before the license expires, it is sent by email with a specific set of details, and some licenses cannot use it at all. We will go through who may ask, what the request must include, and who is excluded, so you know exactly what to do if you are ever in this position.","fact_ids":["sec04-F10","sec04-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Requesting the extension","fact_ids":["sec04-F10","sec04-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Email DMV before expiry.","fact_ids":["sec04-F10","sec04-R04"]},{"text":"Include five details.","fact_ids":["sec04-F10","sec04-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Out-of-state drivers who cannot renew may seek a one-year extension before the license expires. The request is made by email to DMV, and it must include five details: your name, your license number, your birth date, your California residence address, and your out-of-state address. The five-item email packet is the most-missed list in this section, so practice naming all five. Timing matters as well. The request goes in before expiry, not after. If you wait until the license has already expired, you have missed the point of the extension, which is to keep you covered.","fact_ids":["sec04-F10","sec04-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Who is excluded","fact_ids":["sec04-F11","sec04-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Limited-term licenses are barred.","fact_ids":["sec04-F11","sec04-R04"]},{"text":"Others may request it.","fact_ids":["sec04-F11","sec04-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Limited-term licenses are barred from the out-of-state extension. So the rule has two parts. A driver stranded out of state may request a one-year extension by email before expiry, unless the license is limited-term. If your license is limited-term, the extension is not available to you, even if you are out of state and cannot renew. Before relying on the extension, check what kind of license you hold. If it is not limited-term, send the email with all five details before the expiry date. If it is limited-term, the extension simply does not apply.","fact_ids":["sec04-F11","sec04-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u03-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Everyone can extend?","fact_ids":["sec04-F11","sec04-F10","sec04-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Trap: any license can be extended.","fact_ids":["sec04-F11","sec04-F10","sec04-R04"]},{"text":"Truth: limited-term licenses cannot.","fact_ids":["sec04-F11","sec04-F10","sec04-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a trap. Because the extension exists, some drivers assume every license holder who is out of state can use it. That is not the case. Limited-term licenses are barred from the extension. A second trap is waiting too long. The request must be made before the license expires, not after.
